parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans expression, no documented organised targeting or police sweeps, and courts have recently ruled for trans people (Feb 2023 surgery-prerequisite ruling; July 2025 toilet-access ruling striking the birth-sex facility bar). Survey data (59% supporting free gender expression vs 9% opposed; 86% of under-40s backing fair treatment) show moderate, if uneven, acceptance. Against: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime law, so a traveller refused service or assaulted has no practical remedy; trans people report verbal, physical and sexual abuse in public toilets, and the toilet ruling's implementation and reach are undocumented. The 2013 airport customs abuse of a trans traveller is severe and state-implicated but dated and single — weak evidence of present frequency. The 2025 LGBT exclusion report is broad and unquantified. Border handling of foreign markers is an open question, not a documented exposure. Sits just below the 0.65 tier, which requires visitor-facing remedies shown to work.
